title: Scheme action groupoid and equivariant scheme torsor category
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], G a group object in schemes over S [def-sc-group-scheme], and V an S-scheme with a left G-action (a morphism G ×_S V → V satisfying the unit and associativity identities). Define the action category over schemes over S: an object is (T,x:T→V), and an arrow to (T',x') consists of b:T→T' and g:T→G with g·x=x'∘b. Composition has label (g'∘b)g. Define the torsor category: objects are S-schemes P,T, a left G-action on P, an invariant projection p:P→T, fppf locally equivariantly isomorphic over T to G×_S T, and an equivariant map P→V. Here local triviality uses a covering sieve in the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]; for each arrow W→T in that sieve there is an equivariant map G×_S W→P whose square with p and W→T is cartesian. Arrows are equivariant maps P→P' over b:T→T' making that square cartesian and commuting with the maps to V. Both projections remember the actual base scheme and base arrow; composition and identity are scheme composition and identity. Define the trivial-torsor functor by (T,x)↦(G×_S T,(h,t)↦h·x(t)) and (b,g)↦((h,t)↦(hg(t)^{-1},b(t))). Its translation action is (g,(h,t))↦(gh,t). The translation action satisfies the unit and associativity laws, the displayed objects satisfy invariant projection, local triviality and equivariance, and the displayed arrows are cartesian, equivariant, preserve the orbit maps and respect identities and composition. These laws specify the proof fields needed for these actual constructions; no torsor or functor is chosen from an existence assertion.
